title: `SkeletonModifier3D::_process_modification_with_delta()` is called frequently outside of the process
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5 stable v4.5.stable.mono.official [876b29033]
- Reproducible on 4.6 latest (current HEAD of main) 1e9d0ff925563276b5921b9a8b88ebe45680c04a
- [This commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/68ff4e989ae3e24087ee034bdf9619a799871879) is the first one where this issue appears.  However before that the spring bone was not updating at all when calling `.advance()`
- Not relevant to any 4.4 builds (Skeleton3D.MODIFIER_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL not available)

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS - Godot 4.5 stable

### Issue description

Using `Skeleton3D.MODIFIER_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL` with Skeleton3D and manually advancing modifiers using `advance()` appears to work fine until an animation that keyframes any bone in the skeleton is played.  When we do that, modifiers appear to update outside of calls to `advance` and run at full framerate.  (and also act kinda strangely, see the spring bone in attached video)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6e220c2-e72e-4511-bb14-dbe71182da31

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a spring bone simulator on a Skeleton3D
2. Add an AnimationPlayer and animate the Skeleton's position on a loop so we can see the effects of the spring bone in game, make sure to play this animation in _ready()
3. Also in _ready(), set the Skeleton3D's modifier_callback_mode_process to manual like so:
```gdscript
  skeleton.modifier_callback_mode_process = Skeleton3D.MODIFIER_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL
```
4. Manually trigger modifier updates via `advance()`:
```gdscript
const LIMITED_FPS := 5
const TIME_PER_FRAME := 1.0 / float(LIMITED_FPS)

var time_since_last_frame: float = 0.0
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
  time_since_last_frame += delta
  if time_since_last_frame >= TIME_PER_FRAME:

    # Advance the skeleton modifiers at a limited FPS.
    skeleton.advance(time_since_last_frame)
    time_since_last_frame = time_since_last_frame - TIME_PER_FRAME
```
5. Run the project, and note that it works as expected.  Movement at full FPS and SpringBoneSimulator updates at 5FPS
6. Now add any transform keyframe to your looping animation.  Just once at the beginning is fine.

I would expect to see the same results as we before, but now it seems that the springbonesimulator is updating every frame and dragging behind the movement.  Even if we never call `.advance` the spring bone chain appears to update every frame.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test-modifier-callback-manual.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22917301/test-modifier-callback-manual.zip)
